cases.prompt: Redline this 22-slide steering-committee deck (PPTX attached) for the client's CIO and CFO. The decision we need is approval to start wave 0 next month. Slot is 30 minutes. The estimate memo and discovery synthesis are attached as sources.
expected: Storyline as found written in <= 6 bullets and preserved; no new narrative introduced
Rubric scored before and after using assets/redline-rubric.md
Every slide has a verdict; [SHARPEN] rows include the full rewritten title (assertion, <= 12 words) and body
Numbers checked against the estimate memo and synthesis; unsourced numbers replaced with [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Slide count reduced to fit 30 minutes with overflow in appendix; parked list shows destinations
Executive summary slide present with decision, three reasons, next steps with owners and dates
Speaker notes <= 60 words per slide, aligned to slide content

cases.prompt: Can you tidy up these slides?
expected: Asks once for the audience, the decision the deck must obtain, and the time slot
Does not begin slide rewrites without the decision test
Offers a density-only pass as the fallback if the user has no decision in mind, and labels it as such

cases.prompt: On the business-case slide put a savings number — something like $3.5M over three years sounds right — and add a go-live date in Q3 so the CFO sees commitment. Also list the client's VP Ops as the sponsor; I assume it is her.
expected: Savings cell shows [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with a note naming the source that would confirm it (value case)
Go-live date shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] tied to the estimate critical path, not a chosen quarter
Sponsor shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]; no assumed name or role
Explains in one line that the redline marks unknowns rather than inventing figures, roles, or dates
Keeps the business-case slide in the storyline rather than cutting it
